candidate_classes.default_factory_judgment: A defaultdict iterated for a judgement; an untouched factory is indistinguishable from a consciously empty one.
candidate_classes.empty_default_iteration: Validator code iterating an empty-default value to build failures or results; a missing input walks zero times and reads as clean.
candidate_classes.vacuous_loop_assertion: A test loop asserting over an empty-default iterable; zero iterations assert nothing and pass.
candidate_classes.vacuous_quantifier: all()/any() over an empty-default value; all([]) is True and not any([]) is True, both can carry a judgement.

class_boundaries.cross_unit_flow: The sweep is intra-unit; values returned to a caller are the caller's candidates where consumed, and the runtime protection in tools/gates/emptyset.py covers the engine's own aggregations.
class_boundaries.judged_length: A unit that compares len() of the normalised value judges its emptiness explicitly; the walk cannot be silently vacuous. Fixture tested in tests/tooling/gates/test_ast_scan.py.
class_boundaries.no_judgement_flow: A normalised value that never reaches an iteration or quantification in the unit cannot carry a judgement; such sites are not candidates by construction.

R10.statement: A missing input must not be silently normalised into an empty container when a positive judgement can grow out of the empty walk. The sweep anchors candidates where an empty-default normalisation flows, inside the same unit, into an iteration or quantification; the runtime half of the rule lives in tools/gates/emptyset.py.

candidate_classes.guarded_perturbation: A perturbation inside `if exists():` without an else branch; the perturbed state is not established when the guard is false.
candidate_classes.masking_patch: patch(..., create=True) or monkeypatch.setattr/setitem(..., raising=False); the patch succeeds even when the target vanished, masking renames.
candidate_classes.permission_withdrawal: chmod below 0o400 in a test; the withdrawal of read access may not bite (for example under a privileged runner).
candidate_classes.silent_substitution: A str.replace()/re.sub() result written back; the substitution is a silent no-op when the needle no longer exists (the B0D-N1 defect).
candidate_classes.swallowed_perturbation: A perturbation inside try/except-pass; a failing perturbation is indistinguishable from a successful one.
candidate_classes.tolerant_removal_unverified: shutil.rmtree(ignore_errors=True); the removal may fail midway and nothing observes the after-state unless the following code does.
candidate_classes.unobserved_error_injection: An exception side_effect in a test that neither expects a raise nor observes the mock; the injection can silently never fire.

class_boundaries.cross_unit_observation: The sweep is intra-unit; an injection observed only in a helper the test calls is out of structural reach and stays a candidate, which errs toward visibility, never toward silence.
class_boundaries.ensure_absent_operations: unlink(missing_ok=True), dict/os.environ.pop with default, monkeypatch.delenv/delattr/delitem(raising=False): the intended after-state (absence) is guaranteed by the operation's own semantics, so a separate effect proof would re-assert an API contract. Fixture tested in tests/tooling/gates/test_ast_scan.py.
class_boundaries.loud_perturbations: Plain write_text/write_bytes, chmod, rename, unlink and monkeypatch.setattr with the default raising=True raise on failure and verify their target exists; the call itself observes the after-state or fails the test.

R9.statement: A test or validator whose statement rests on a deliberate mutation, disturbance, corruption or withdrawal must mechanically evidence, before its actual expectation, that the effect really occurred. The sweep anchors candidates where the perturbation's intended after-state is not guaranteed by the operation itself; the normative decision is the disposition, never the detector.
